metadata.case_name: WU CHUI SHAN STELLA v. HOSPITAL AUTHORITY ON BEHALF OF QUEEN ELIZABETH HOSPITAL

plaintiff.occupation_before: Registered nurse employed by the Hospital Authority at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Registered nurse employed by the Hospital Authority at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
plaintiff.education_level: Three years of nursing training at the Princess Margaret Hospital (starting 1990)

source: They took the view that she had sprained her back.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: degenerative disc disease with bulging at L4-5 and L5-S1
source: Disc prolapses are demonstrated at the L4-5 and the L5-S1 level. At the L4-5 level this is left lateral in location indenting the thecal sac and at the lateral recess. At the L5-S1 level, the disc prolapse is mainly midline obliterating the epidural fat with no significant indentation onto the thecal sac.
We consider that the disc pathology should be regarded as degenerative disc disease with bulging, with no significant impingement onto the spinal thecal sac or nerve roots.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: leg pain (probable consequence of nerve root irritation at L4-L5)
restriction of work as a nurse by avoidance of bending and lifting

treatments_received: admission to the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology at QEH

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: She used to run, play badminton, roller-skating, and squash and do aerobics and go hiking, but she can no longer do any of these things.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: She still cannot lift heavy objects. She cannot squat, for instance to work the handle to lift a patient’s bedhead; she cannot wear high heels for longer than a few minutes without suffering from left leg and low back pain; sometimes she cannot bend.
Her work as a nurse is severely restricted by the avoidance of bending and lifting and she alleges risk of dismissal and loss of earning capacity.
